S8.01.note: The button uses the class primary-button. I did not check the colours or the label contrast.
steps: Click the gear icon named Settings in the chat header.
Click Runtime in the left list.
Look at the Open config.toml button and compare it with the other buttons on the page: it should look like the main action.
S8.01.where: Chat header > Settings (gear) > Runtime > Open config.toml

S8.02.note: The button uses the class secondary-button. I did not check how its outline looks.
steps: Click the gear icon named Settings in the chat header.
Stay on General and find the row labelled Model preference.
Look at the Choose button beside the model box. It should look less strong than the main buttons, such as Open config.toml under Runtime.
S8.02.where: Chat header > Settings (gear) > General > Model preference > Choose

S8.03.needs: a workspace folder open; an AGI runtime that is set up so the agent asks for approval
S8.03.note: The danger style is the class approval-card__action--danger (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts line 982). Abort turn is also set to the danger style. Whether a card shows depends on the approval setting, which I did not check.
steps: Open a workspace folder in VS Code and type a task that makes AGI change a file, such as creating a new text file, in the message box at the bottom of the chat.
Press Enter and wait for an approval card to appear in the chat.
Look at the Deny button. It should look red (a warning colour) and be clearly different from the approve button.
S8.03.where: Chat > send a task that needs a tool approval > Deny on the approval card

S8.04.needs: none; VoiceOver for the name check
S8.04.note: Each icon button has an aria-label and a title in webviewContent.ts (lines 2928 to 2942).
steps: Open the AGI chat view in the sidebar.
Look at the row of icon-only buttons at the top right of the chat header.
Turn on VoiceOver (Cmd+F5), move it over each icon, and listen for the name: Sessions, Settings, New chat, More actions.
S8.04.where: Chat header, top right: the icon buttons Sessions (clock), Settings (gear), New chat (plus), and More actions (three dots)

S8.07.note: These are navigation groups (role group, labelled by their heading), not a toolbar. I did not find a separate button group in the chat header.
steps: Click the gear icon named Settings in the chat header.
Look at the left list. Under the label Workspace there are General, Runtime, Instructions & editor and Usage & billing.
Under Integrations there are MCP servers, Hooks, Plugins and Skills. Under Account there is Cloud account. Each group has its own label.
S8.07.where: Chat header > Settings (gear) > left list with the group labels Workspace, Integrations and Account

S8.08.needs: a reply that contains a link (the agent decides this)
S8.08.note: Links are made by markdown-it with linkify on (apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts line 18). I did not check the click handler that opens the link.
steps: Send a message that asks AGI for a web page address with a link in the answer.
Look at the reply. A link should be underlined or coloured like a link.
Click the link and check that the browser opens the page.
S8.08.where: Chat > a reply that contains a web address shown as a link

S8.09.note: The only labelled single-line text box found in the settings is the Model preference box, and the code marks it readonly (settingsWebviewContent.ts lines 1346 to 1357). Expected asks for an input, so a readonly box may not match.
steps: Click the gear icon named Settings in the chat header.
Stay on General and look at the box under the label Model preference.
Compare with Expected: the box is a single-line text box with a visible label. Click into it and try to type.
S8.09.where: Chat header > Settings (gear) > General > Model preference (text box beside the Choose button)

S8.10.note: Which key adds a new line depends on the Enter setting (composerKeys in webviewContent.ts lines 5088 to 5094). By default Enter sends the message; I did not check the default setting value.
steps: Click in the message box, which says Describe a task….
Type one line of text, then press Cmd+Enter.
Type a second line and look for it on a new line in the box. The box should grow up to a limit.
S8.10.where: Chat > message box at the bottom (placeholder Describe a task…)

S8.11.note: The box is type search with a placeholder and aria-label. I did not check whether it filters as you type or only on Enter.
steps: Click the Sessions icon in the chat header.
Click the box named Search sessions at the top of the sheet.
Type part of the title of an older chat and look at the list. Only matching sessions should stay.
S8.11.where: Chat header > Sessions (clock) > search box Search sessions

S8.12.needs: none; use a test string, not a real key
S8.12.note: The input uses password true (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts line 1267), so the typed text should be masked.
steps: Open the Command Palette with Cmd+Shift+P.
Type Set API Key and choose Code: Set API Key.
Type a short test string (not a real key) and look at the box. The typed characters should be hidden.
S8.12.where: Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > Code: Set API Key

S8.16.note: The control is a checkbox given role switch (settingsWebviewContent.ts line 2437).
steps: Click the gear icon named Settings in the chat header.
Stay on General and find the row labelled Extended thinking.
Click its switch once. Look at the switch: it should slide to the other state. Close and reopen Settings to see whether the new state stayed.
S8.16.where: Chat header > Settings (gear) > General > Extended thinking

S8.17.needs: a Cloud account to see Cloud sessions (I did not check what the Cloud list shows without one)
S8.17.note: The same two buttons are also used as tabs in S8.31.
steps: Click the Sessions icon in the chat header.
Look at the two joined buttons Local and Cloud at the top.
Click Cloud, then look at which one looks selected and at the list below. Click Local to go back.
S8.17.where: Chat header > Sessions (clock) > Local | Cloud at the top of the sheet

S8.18.note: The same choice is also available from the Command Palette as Code: Choose Agent Mode (apps/extension-vscode/package.json line 133).
steps: Click the gear icon named Settings in the chat header.
Stay on General and find the row labelled Agent mode.
Click its dropdown, choose a different mode, and check that the shown value changes. Close and reopen Settings to see whether it stayed.
S8.18.where: Chat header > Settings (gear) > General > Agent mode

S8.19.note: The @ trigger is in webviewContent.ts around line 8540. I did not check the keyboard behaviour beyond the arrow and Escape keys in the handler near line 5906.
steps: Open a workspace folder and click the message box.
Type @. A list with the title Workspace files and symbols opens above the box.
Type a few letters to narrow the list, press the Down arrow to move, and press Enter to pick one. Check that the picked item appears in the message.
S8.19.where: Chat > message box at the bottom > type @

S8.22.note: The input is type number with min 0 and max 500 (settingsWebviewContent.ts lines 1481 to 1495).
steps: Click the gear icon named Settings in the chat header.
Stay on General and find the box labelled Context lines.
Click the box, then use the Up and Down arrow keys or the small spinner arrows. The number should change, and it should stop at 0 and at 500.
S8.22.where: Chat header > Settings (gear) > General > Context lines

S8.29.needs: a workspace folder open; a file to attach
S8.29.note: Expected says choose files from the device, but the menu item says workspace files. The code also has an Attach file… action that posts openFilePicker (webviewContent.ts line 6601), and I did not confirm which one shows a native file dialog. No HTML file input was found.
steps: Open a workspace folder, then click the + button named Attach or use tools.
Look at the menu titled Add context and click Attach workspace files.
Check that a way to choose files opens (a file dialog or a list). Compare with Expected: choosing files from the device.
S8.29.where: Chat > + (Attach or use tools) at the bottom left of the message box > Attach workspace files

S8.30.needs: a file to upload; a workspace folder open
S8.30.note: The drag-over style is composer-card dragover (webviewContent.ts lines 2817 to 2820); the drop handler is near line 7720.
steps: Open a file in Finder and slowly drag it over the message box.
Look for the box border to turn teal and the box to get a thicker ring while the file is over it.
Drop the file and look for a file chip in the strip above the box.
S8.30.where: Chat > drag a file from Finder onto the message box at the bottom (placeholder Describe a task…)

S8.31.needs: a Cloud account for the Cloud list to have content
S8.31.note: The tab group has role tablist and each button has role tab with aria-selected (webviewContent.ts lines 3036 to 3038). I did not check the arrow-key behaviour.
steps: Click the Sessions icon in the chat header.
Look at the Local and Cloud tabs at the top of the sheet.
Click Cloud and check that the selected tab looks active and that the list changes. Click Local to go back.
S8.31.where: Chat header > Sessions (clock) > Local and Cloud tabs

S8.33.needs: an error message in the chat (I did not find a fixed way to cause one)
S8.33.note: The Details row appears only when an error has extra detail (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts lines 4569 to 4580). The toggle is a button with aria-expanded.
steps: Find a chat message that shows an error with extra text.
Click the row labelled Details and check that the extra text opens below it.
Click it again and check that the text hides and the arrow turns back.
S8.33.where: Chat > a message that shows an error > Details

S8.34.note: The menu has role menu and menu items (webviewContent.ts lines 3198 to 3221). I did not check the keyboard behaviour in the code.
steps: Click the + button named Attach or use tools.
Check that a menu titled Add context opens above the box with items such as Attach workspace files, Selection and Open editors.
Press Escape or click outside the menu and check that it closes.
S8.34.where: Chat > + (Attach or use tools) at the bottom left of the message box

S8.35.needs: a code file open with text selected; an AGI runtime set up for a real answer
S8.35.note: The menu entry is in the editor/context group of apps/extension-vscode/package.json (around line 980). I did not check what happens without a runtime.
steps: Open a code file in the editor and select a few lines.
Right-click (or Control-click on a Mac trackpad) inside the selection.
Look for Code: Explain Selection in the menu and click it. Check that the chat opens with an explanation request.
S8.35.where: Editor > select some code > right-click the selection > Code: Explain Selection

S8.37.note: The tooltips come from title attributes, so they show on hover only; the code does not add focus tooltips.
steps: Move the mouse over the gear icon in the chat header and wait about one second.
Check that a small label Settings appears.
Repeat on the plus icon (New chat) and the clock icon (Sessions).
S8.37.where: Chat header > hover over the icon buttons Sessions, Settings and New chat

S8.38.note: The popover has role menu and aria-expanded on its trigger (webviewContent.ts lines 3288 and 3361). I did not confirm the Escape and outside-click dismissal in the code.
steps: Click the model name button, which shows Auto by default.
Check that a menu labelled Select model opens above the box.
Press Escape, then click outside the menu, and check that it closes each time.
S8.38.where: Chat composer, bottom row > the model name button (default Auto) and the Mode and reasoning effort button

S8.40.needs: a running task that sets the attention state
S8.40.note: The badge is VS Code's view badge set in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/sidebarProvider.ts (around line 188). I did not check which events set it (attentionBadge.ts).
steps: Hide the AGI chat view, or open another Activity Bar view so the AGI view is not visible.
Start a task that needs your attention, such as one that ends or asks for approval.
Look at the AGI icon in the Activity Bar for a small count badge, then open the AGI view and check that the badge clears.
S8.40.where: Activity Bar (left edge of VS Code) > the AGI chat icon, which can show a count badge

S8.42.note: I found no visible avatar in the code. The only author marker is visually hidden text (prependAuthor, webviewContent.ts line 4934), so Expected's visual part may not be met.
steps: Turn on VoiceOver (Cmd+F5).
Send a short message in the chat, then wait for the reply.
Move VoiceOver over your message and then the reply. Listen for You said: and AGI replied: before each message text.
S8.42.where: Chat messages, heard with VoiceOver (no visible avatar found)

S8.43.needs: none; the review may ask for sign-in first (not checked in code)
S8.43.note: The Plan usage bar only shows when the account has plan usage data; that was not verified at runtime.
steps: Open any code file and select a few lines.
Right-click the selection and choose Code: Code Review.
Look at the notification titled Code: Running Code Review… in the corner: it should show progress and a cancel option.
Optional: open the settings with Code: Open Settings, click Usage & billing, and look at the Plan usage bar.
S8.43.where: Select code in an editor, right-click the selection > Code: Code Review (also in the Command Palette as Code: Code Review). While it runs, a notification titled Code: Running Code Review… shows progress. A second progress bar is at Code: Open Settings > Usage & billing > Plan usage (role progressbar, aria-label "AGI Cloud plan usage").

S8.45.needs: a pending change from the assistant
S8.45.note: The notification text comes from describeDiffScope, whose wording was not read. Whether it auto-dismisses is decided by VS Code, not this code. Another toast (memory off) also exists at commandSetup.ts line 254, not tested.
steps: Make sure the assistant has a pending change waiting for review in a file.
Open the Command Palette and run Code: Reject All Diffs (All Files).
Confirm the dialog that asks about the reject.
Look for a transient notification with the message about the discarded changes and a Restore discarded button; it should go away on its own and not block the editor.
S8.45.where: Command Palette > Code: Reject All Diffs (All Files), then confirm; a notification with a Restore discarded button appears.

labels.text: Older messages may be dropped; start a new chat to keep full context.

S8.46.needs: a long chat that reaches the context warning level
S8.46.note: The exact warning percent comes from configuration and was not checked; the error block at webviewContent.ts line 4569 is a disclosure inside an error, not this alert.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar and open Chat.
Keep sending messages in one chat until it uses a large share of the model's context.
Look just above the message box for the note that starts with: This chat has used N% of the model's context.
Check that the note is announced as a status message (it has role status) and that it disappears when the chat is cleared.
S8.46.where: AGI Code (Activity Bar icon) > Chat > the note above the message box, once a chat is long.

S8.47.needs: an account at its Managed Cloud limit or on a plan without Cloud access
S8.47.note: The strip is hidden unless the plan state triggers it, and the Upgrade button label changes to Manage billing when a paid plan needs attention. The exact trigger was not tested.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar and open Chat.
Find the full-width usage strip with a cloud icon, meter and an Upgrade button.
Check that the strip shows the plan usage text and the Upgrade button, and that its text matches the account's plan state.
Optional: collapse it with its close control and check that it becomes a small pill.
S8.47.where: AGI Code (Activity Bar icon) > Chat > the usage strip with the cloud icon, meter text and an Upgrade button.

labels.text: Ask about your code or describe a change.

S8.49.note: A variant class empty-state--has-recents exists for chats with recent history; what it shows was not checked.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar.
Open Chat with no messages yet (start a new chat).
Look in the message area for the heading Start a conversation.
Read the line under it: Ask about your code or describe a change.
S8.49.where: AGI Code (Activity Bar icon) > Chat, with no messages in a new chat.

S8.50.needs: a way to switch off the network connection
S8.50.note: Retry shows only when the error is marked retryable and a send exists; the headline comes from the error type, so its exact wording is not fixed in the code. The view-level Try again button (runtimeRetryBtn in webviewContent.ts) is a separate recovery action.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar and open Chat.
Turn off the Wi-Fi or network connection.
Type a short message and send it.
Look in the transcript for an error block with a headline and a Retry button; turn the network back on, press Retry and compare with Expected.
S8.50.where: AGI Code (Activity Bar icon) > Chat > send a message while the connection is down; an error block appears in the transcript with a Retry button.
